history.summary: One of Nagpur's most revered Ganesha shrines. The swayambhu (self-manifested) idol was discovered during dynamite blasting of the Sitaburdi hill for railway construction; it is believed to have grown in size over time. The early shrine was a modest tin-shade platform. Adjoining land was acquired in 1965; the Defence wing held the site and renovations began in 1970. Temple construction started in 1978 and completed in 1984 with public donations (with 20,000 sq ft of additional land granted by the Defence Ministry). Regarded as a Jagruta Devasthan (spiritually 'awake' shrine) and counted among Vidarbha's Ashtavinayakas; visited by cricketers such as Sachin Tendulkar before matches.

name: Shri Ganesh Tekdi Mandir
town_description: The temple crowns a small hill ('tekdi' in Marathi) at Sitabuldi, in the heart of Nagpur city, on Ganesh Tekdi Road within walking distance of Nagpur Railway Station; the shrine is set among preserved trees.

travel.airport: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport, ~9 km southwest
travel.road: Ganesh Tekdi Road, Sitabuldi; parking on the road; two/four-wheeler puja offered in the premises for a fee

visitor_information.best_time: Ganesh Chaturthi (Aug-Sep) and winter; expect long queues on Sankashti Chaturthis
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM daily (some sources say 5:00 AM to 11:00 PM or till midnight during festivals - verify); aartis at 6:30 AM, 12:30 PM and 6:30 PM followed by modak prasad
